newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters wants to show two agreements to caucus.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters wants to show two agreements to caucus.

text.p: New Zealand First leader Winston Peters wants to present his party with two separate coalition agreements to help it decide between the National and Labour parties, Radio New Zealand said.

It quoted Peters as saying 68 policies had been up for negotiation in marathon coalition talks, and a great number sorted out, but major areas such as the economy and superannuation needed further discussion.

"Both National and Labour, I would imagine, would go to their caucus with a set of understandings with which they can negotiate with their own caucus. We need to be in the same position -- twice over, in this case," Peters said.
The next formal talks with National and Labour are due next Tuesday, but nine informal groups are continuing detailed negotiations in major areas, he said.
New Zealand First was left holding the balance of power after the October 12 election.
